activities.title: Homeostasis & negative feedback
activities.description: Explore a regulated variable responding to a constant disturbance.
activities.limits: Linear single-variable feedback model; real regulation involves delays, saturation and multiple signals. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a persistent disturbance can leave an offset from the set point.

activities.title: Tissues: structure & function
activities.description: Compare major tissue classes and their characteristic organization.
activities.equation: Organization of cells and extracellular material supports tissue function.
activities.limits: A conceptual arrangement, not a histology image or classification algorithm. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain one structure–function relationship without using a cell-city analogy.

activities.title: Cell geometry & exchange
activities.description: Relate cell radius to membrane area and cellular volume.
activities.limits: Ideal spherical cell without folds; exchange also depends on transport proteins, gradients and metabolism. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why small size can help exchange without imposing one universal size limit.

activities.title: Skin layers & injury depth
activities.description: Inspect a layered schematic and identify which tissues a selected depth reaches.
activities.equation: Epidermis is epithelial; dermis is connective tissue; hypodermis lies below the skin proper.
activities.limits: Layer thicknesses and structures are schematic, not a prediction of wound severity. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why dermal injury can involve blood vessels whereas the epidermis is avascular.

activities.title: Heat transfer & cooling
activities.description: Compare passive heat loss with a simplified cooling curve.
activities.limits: Passive object/surface model; not a whole-body thermoregulation or core-temperature prediction. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain the role of temperature difference in passive heat transfer.

activities.title: Repair stages & overlapping processes
activities.description: Explore dominant processes in a schematic wound-repair sequence.
activities.equation: Hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodeling overlap in time.
activities.limits: Stage selection is conceptual; healing does not follow a universal fixed timetable. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Connect a repair process to its cellular participants.

activities.title: Bone remodeling balance
activities.description: Compare formation and resorption in a relative bone-mass bookkeeping model.
activities.limits: Fixed rates and relative units; no prediction of fracture risk, mineral density or clinical treatment. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Connect osteoblast and osteoclast activity to net structural change.

activities.title: Fracture patterns & structure
activities.description: Compare illustrative transverse, oblique, spiral and comminuted patterns.
activities.equation: Pattern describes the break geometry; open/closed status describes communication with the exterior.
activities.limits: Stylized long-bone sketches, not radiographs or a diagnosis. Pattern does not determine every injury mechanism. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Distinguish pattern, location and open/closed status.

activities.title: Skeletal levers & torque
activities.description: Calculate muscle force needed to balance a load about a joint.
activities.limits: Static planar torque balance; limb weight, changing angle and co-contraction are omitted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a short muscle moment arm can require a large force.

activities.title: Sarcomere overlap & active tension
activities.description: Change length and distinguish overlap from filament shortening.
activities.equation: Active tension depends on actin–myosin overlap; filaments slide without shortening.
activities.limits: Illustrative piecewise length–tension curve; not measured muscle data. Passive tension is omitted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain what changes in the I band, H zone and filament lengths during shortening.

activities.title: Motor-unit recruitment & force
activities.description: Compare recruited units with force output under equal-unit assumptions.
activities.equation: Total force = unit count × recruited fraction × unit force × retained fraction
activities.limits: Equal independent motor units and linear addition; real motor units differ and recruitment order is not simulated. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Distinguish motor-unit recruitment from increasing firing frequency.

activities.title: Twitch summation
activities.description: Compare overlapping force pulses after repeated stimuli.
activities.limits: Linear pulse superposition, without a physiological force ceiling; not a calibrated tetanus or calcium model. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a second stimulus can add force before complete relaxation.

activities.title: Action potential & threshold
activities.description: Trigger an illustrative all-or-none waveform while separating stimulus size from spike amplitude.
activities.equation: In this example, reaching −55 mV triggers a fixed-shape spike.
activities.limits: Schematic waveform and fixed threshold, not Hodgkin–Huxley channel kinetics. Neuronal thresholds vary. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a stronger suprathreshold stimulus does not simply create a taller action potential.

activities.title: Synaptic integration
activities.description: Add simplified excitatory and inhibitory effects before threshold comparison.
activities.limits: Linear voltage sum at one moment. Real synapses involve conductances, reversal potentials, timing and spatial attenuation. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how excitatory and inhibitory inputs can affect whether threshold is reached.

activities.title: Reflex arc & lesions
activities.description: Trace a sensory-to-motor pathway and explore a blocked link.
activities.equation: Receptor → sensory neuron → CNS integration → motor neuron → effector
activities.limits: Generic reflex arc; some reflexes have additional interneurons and modulation. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Predict where information fails to reach the next component after a lesion.

activities.title: Thin lens & image formation
activities.description: Relate object distance to focal length and image distance.
activities.limits: Single thin converging lens in air; the eye is a multi-surface optical system with accommodation. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why near objects require a change in focusing power for a fixed retinal distance.

activities.title: Sound intensity & decibels
activities.description: Connect a logarithmic sound level to an intensity ratio.
activities.limits: Intensity ratio, not a direct perceived-loudness scale; frequency response and hearing physiology are omitted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a 20 dB difference is not twice the intensity of a 10 dB difference.

activities.title: Sensory adaptation
activities.description: Compare a transient response with a sustained response to a constant stimulus.
activities.limits: Empirical exponential teaching response, not a particular receptor’s measured firing rate. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why adaptation does not mean all receptors always become silent.

activities.title: Hormone receptors & occupancy
activities.description: Distinguish circulating concentration, receptor occupancy and biological response.
activities.limits: Independent identical receptors at equilibrium. Downstream amplification and regulation are not calculated. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how receptor abundance or affinity can change sensitivity.

activities.title: Hypothalamic–pituitary–target feedback
activities.description: Trace an endocrine axis and distinguish target hormones from upstream signals.
activities.equation: Target-gland hormones can inhibit hypothalamic and pituitary secretion.
activities.limits: Qualitative axis with intact negative feedback; actual concentrations, pulsatility and disorders are not predicted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how a target-gland change can alter upstream signals.

activities.title: Hormone removal & half-life
activities.description: Explore exponential clearance after an isolated hormone input.
activities.limits: First-order clearance without additional secretion; distribution and receptor-mediated effects are omitted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a half-life removes a fraction rather than a fixed amount.

activities.title: Cardiac output
activities.description: Connect heart rate and stroke volume to flow per minute.
activities.limits: Independent entered HR and SV; actual filling, contractility and regulation couple these variables. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why raising heart rate does not guarantee unlimited cardiac output.

activities.title: Vessel radius & flow resistance
activities.description: Compare radius changes in a Poiseuille-style vessel model.
activities.limits: Rigid straight cylindrical tube, constant viscosity and laminar steady flow; circulation is branching, pulsatile and compliant. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why a small radius change can strongly affect resistance.

activities.title: Ventricular volumes & ejection fraction
activities.description: Distinguish end-diastolic volume, end-systolic volume and stroke volume.
activities.limits: Volume accounting with a schematic cycle; EF alone does not establish function or a diagnosis. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain the relationship between stroke volume and ejection fraction.

activities.title: Hemoglobin oxygen binding
activities.description: Explore a Hill-shaped oxygen-dissociation curve and a P50 shift.
activities.limits: Empirical binding model; real temperature, pH, CO₂ and 2,3-BPG effects are represented only indirectly by P50. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how a right shift affects saturation at a fixed partial pressure.

activities.title: ABO antigens & red-cell compatibility
activities.description: Compare a red-cell donor antigen set with recipient ABO antibodies.
activities.equation: Donor red-cell antigens must not be targeted by recipient ABO antibodies.
activities.limits: ABO red-cell teaching logic only; Rh, other antigens, plasma compatibility and laboratory crossmatching are omitted. Not transfusion guidance. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why compatibility depends on which component is transferred.

activities.title: Blood composition & hematocrit
activities.description: Separate red-cell volume fraction from total blood volume.
activities.equation: Red-cell volume = hematocrit fraction × sample volume
activities.limits: Simple packed-volume accounting; buffy coat and plasma contributions are combined in the remainder. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why hematocrit and hemoglobin concentration are related but different quantities.

activities.title: Capillary fluid exchange
activities.description: Explore a simplified classic Starling pressure balance.
activities.limits: Classic simplified balance. Modern microvascular exchange includes endothelial glycocalyx and lymphatic return; this is not a full tissue-fluid model. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how hydrostatic and oncotic forces differ.

activities.title: Primary & secondary immune responses
activities.description: Compare schematic antigen-specific responses with and without memory.
activities.equation: Memory can reduce response delay and increase antigen-specific response.
activities.limits: Illustrative dimensionless curves, not antibody titers or protection predictions. Real immunity depends on pathogen and host. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Connect memory cells to a changed response while avoiding the claim of guaranteed immunity.

activities.title: Innate & adaptive cooperation
activities.description: Trace antigen handling and examine the function of a selected immune-cell role.
activities.equation: Antigen presentation and signaling coordinate cellular and humoral responses.
activities.limits: Selected canonical roles; real cells have additional functions and pathways. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Distinguish antibody production from killing an infected cell.

activities.title: Minute & alveolar ventilation
activities.description: Separate total airflow from airflow reaching exchange regions.
activities.limits: Constant entered volumes; anatomical and physiological dead space can differ. No clinical adequacy is inferred. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why rapid shallow breathing can give different alveolar ventilation from deep slower breathing.

activities.title: Lung volumes & capacities
activities.description: Compose capacities from component volumes and distinguish residual volume.
activities.limits: Entered illustrative volumes. Simple spirometry does not directly measure residual volume. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why vital capacity does not equal total lung capacity.

activities.title: Gas exchange & diffusion distance
activities.description: Explore area, pressure gradient and barrier thickness in a relative Fick model.
activities.equation: Relative diffusion rate = area ratio × gradient ratio / thickness ratio
activities.limits: Constant diffusion coefficient; perfusion, ventilation mismatch and gas binding are not included. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why thickening an exchange barrier changes flux without changing its direction.

activities.title: Digestion & nutrient energy
activities.description: Estimate energy from macronutrient amounts and separate digestion from absorption.
activities.limits: General Atwater estimates; actual digestibility and specific foods vary. No dietary recommendation is provided. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why equal masses of macronutrients contribute different estimated energy.

activities.title: Digestive enzymes & saturation
activities.description: Compare enzyme abundance and substrate saturation in an ideal rate model.
activities.limits: Single-enzyme steady-state curve; pH, enzyme activation, digestion time and intestinal mixing are omitted. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why doubling substrate does not always double digestion rate.

activities.title: Bile flow & fat processing
activities.description: Trace bile from liver through storage or direct delivery to the duodenum.
activities.equation: Bile supports emulsification and micelle formation; it is not a digestive enzyme.
activities.limits: Simplified route schematic. A cystic-duct block prevents gallbladder flow but does not necessarily block liver-to-duodenum flow. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Distinguish bile production, storage and delivery.

activities.title: Glomerular filtration forces
activities.description: Relate a simplified net filtration pressure to a supplied filtration coefficient.
activities.limits: Simplified fixed-coefficient model; negligible capsule oncotic pressure, no autoregulation. Negative net pressure is outside this forward-filtration view. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how hydrostatic and oncotic forces affect filtration.

activities.title: Renal clearance
activities.description: Calculate the plasma-equivalent volume cleared of a substance each minute.
activities.limits: Clearance is substance-specific and is not always GFR. Filtration, secretion and reabsorption affect interpretation. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why clearance is a virtual volume rate rather than the actual urine volume.

activities.title: Nephron transport & water handling
activities.description: Compare loop segments and ADH-dependent collecting-duct permeability.
activities.equation: Descending limb favors water movement; ascending limb removes salt with low water permeability.
activities.limits: Qualitative nephron segment model; no quantitative medullary gradient or urine osmolality prediction. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how an osmotic gradient and permeability work together.

activities.title: Respiratory & renal acid–base contributions
activities.description: Relate bicarbonate and carbon dioxide in a simplified physiological buffer equation.
activities.limits: Approximate bicarbonate buffer relation with supplied values; compensatory responses and patient interpretation are not modeled. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how respiratory CO₂ and renal bicarbonate changes can influence the same buffer system.

activities.title: Gametogenesis & chromosome accounting
activities.description: Compare chromosome and DNA content through meiosis.
activities.equation: Replication doubles DNA; meiosis reduces homologous chromosome sets.
activities.limits: Chromosome count is by centromeres per cell. Species values are illustrative unless n=23 is chosen for humans. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Distinguish chromosome number from chromatid number and DNA content.

activities.title: Reproductive structures & transport
activities.description: Trace gamete transport and distinguish fertilization from implantation.
activities.equation: Typical fertilization occurs in the uterine tube; implantation occurs in the uterus.
activities.limits: Canonical structural routes; not a fertility or timing prediction. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain the function of each structure along the selected route.

activities.title: Early development & differentiation
activities.description: Separate cell division, implantation and tissue differentiation in a schematic sequence.
activities.equation: Cleavage increases cell number without comparable overall conceptus growth; gastrulation establishes germ layers.
activities.limits: Schematic stage sequence without fixed day assignments; no pregnancy or embryo-viability prediction. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why increasing cell number and differentiation are different processes.

activities.title: Calcium regulation & remodeling
activities.description: Connect a simplified low-calcium signal to PTH-regulated processes.
activities.equation: PTH can promote renal calcium retention, calcitriol activation and effects that increase calcium release from bone.
activities.limits: Qualitative intact-feedback model; no concentration, time course or treatment prediction. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain how multiple organs can participate in restoring one regulated variable.

activities.title: Insulin & glucagon feedback
activities.description: Trace complementary hormone responses to glucose availability.
activities.equation: Insulin favors storage and glucose uptake in responsive tissues; glucagon favors hepatic glucose output.
activities.limits: Qualitative healthy-feedback example. Glucose transport is tissue-specific; insulin is not required for every cell’s uptake. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain coordinated liver, muscle and adipose responses without claiming all cells use the same transporter.

activities.title: Oxygen content & delivery
activities.description: Separate hemoglobin-bound oxygen, dissolved oxygen and blood flow.
activities.limits: Illustrative content relation; saturation is a fraction in the equation. No tissue consumption, extraction or clinical adequacy is inferred. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why normal partial pressure alone does not establish normal oxygen delivery.

activities.title: Filtered load & transport maximum
activities.description: Compare filtration, capped reabsorption and excretion for a model solute.
activities.limits: Sharp transport cap with no secretion or nephron heterogeneity; actual threshold can show splay rather than a sharp corner. Educational physiology; not a patient-specific or diagnostic model.
activities.goal: Explain why excretion can begin when a transport system saturates.
